title: How Big Is a Billion?
objective: After this level you can picture the difference between a thousand, a million and a billion using seconds of time.
summary: A billion is a thousand millions. Counted in seconds, a thousand is about 17 minutes, a million about 11 and a half days, and a billion almost 32 years.

cards.headline: A million and a billion sound like neighbors. In seconds, they're decades apart.
cards.body: Our ears hear "million" and "billion" as one small step. Counting them out in seconds shows just how big that step is.

cards.headline: Each step is 1,000 times bigger
cards.body: A thousand is 1,000. A million is a thousand thousands. A billion is a thousand millions: 1,000,000,000. The metric prefixes climb the same ladder, with kilo for thousand, mega for million and giga for billion. Each rung multiplies by a thousand, which makes a billion a million times bigger than a thousand.

cards.headline: Why it matters in the news
cards.body: A day has 86,400 seconds, so a million of them is gone in under two weeks. A billion takes almost 32 years. Next time a headline puts $5 million next to $5 billion, picture the seconds: a short vacation against three decades of birthdays. The billion isn't a bit bigger. It's 1,000 times bigger.

mascot.line: Don't memorize the exact days. Keep the picture: a million seconds is a vacation, a billion is decades.

cards.headline: Big numbers: pictured
learned: Each step up is 1,000 times bigger
A million seconds: about 11 and a half days
Kilo, mega, giga: thousand, million, billion

questions.explanation: A billion seconds is almost 32 years; a million is only about 11 and a half days.

questions.prompt: Match each count of seconds with how long it lasts.
questions.explanation: 1,000 seconds is about 17 minutes, 1 million is about 11 and a half days, 1 billion is almost 32 years, and 1 trillion is about 31,700 years.

questions.prompt: Using Level 2's divide-and-move-the-decimal method, a million is what percent of a billion?

options.rationale: That would make a billion 100 millions.

questions.explanation: A million is 1 out of every 1,000 in a billion: 1 ÷ 1,000 = 0.001, which is 0.1%.
